title: StrataSpecItem
description: A specification-grounded evaluation item. Extends TrialPrompt with the externally-specified computation: which attributes the spec REQUIRES the model to use, and which it FORBIDS. Serves pillars 1 and 2 from a single object.

source.description: Provenance of the specification itself — the protocol or guideline that defines the correct computation.

target_token.description: Single canonical token for attribution. Calibrate the surface form against a forward pass rather than assuming it: being a single token and being the token the model emits are different questions. Under a chat template ending in a newline, Gemma-3 emits the BARE form ('Yes'=10784); the leading-space ' Yes' (8438) is a single token but carries ~0 probability. See data/ecog_v0_results_READOUT_BUG.md.

answer_token_variants.description: All case/space variants, for probability aggregation during evaluation ONLY. Never used for attribution.

required_conditions.description: PILLAR 1. The conjunction the spec requires. Each must have an identifiable causal representative in the circuit or the item scores a completeness failure.

span.description: [start, end] char offsets in prompt — the text that must be attended to

contrast_variant.description: Prompt with this condition alone flipped. Basis of the contrastive protocol.

decisive.description: Whether flipping this condition alone flips the correct answer

intermediate.description: PILLAR 1 under ADR-0004. The clinical abstraction the criterion is written in — ECOG grade, creatinine clearance, NYHA class — as distinct from the raw patient facts. Recovery of this variable, not criterion-node search, is what pillar 1 now measures: a model may reach the right eligibility answer without ever computing the intermediate the spec is defined over. Vignettes vary only the clinical description; the intermediate and threshold stay fixed, or the probe learns sick-versus-well instead.

variable.description: Stable slug, e.g. 'ecog_performance_status', 'creatinine_clearance', 'nyha_class'. One intermediate per item.

value_type.description: Drives the readout. 'ordinal' and 'categorical' are scored as a distribution over a small value set; 'continuous' is NOT — see elicitation.answer_surface.

values.description: Admissible values, in order for ordinal (e.g. ['0','1','2','3','4'], ['I','II','III','IV']). Omit for continuous.

true_value.description: The adjudicated value for this patient. Ground truth for the recovery test.

threshold.description: The cut the criterion applies to this intermediate. Kept separate from the value so the same stimulus can be scored against different protocols.

text.description: As written in the protocol, e.g. 'ECOG <= 1'.

decisive.description: Whether this intermediate's value alone settles eligibility for this item. Non-decisive items still test recovery but cannot test routing.

ambiguous.description: The VALUE is contestable (e.g. 0-vs-1) while eligibility may not be. Ambiguous items are excluded from headline recovery accuracy and reported separately; scoring a contestable value as wrong invents a recovery failure.

contestable_values.description: The defensible alternatives when ambiguous is true.

uses_defining_vocabulary.description: Whether the narrative names the intermediate or its scale wording. MUST be false for a recovery item — if true the item tests lookup, not recovery.

defining_vocabulary.description: Terms the narrative must avoid for this variable, e.g. ['ECOG', 'performance status', 'Karnofsky']. Checked mechanically.

lexical_distance.description: Distance from the published scale wording. 'verbatim' items are controls; 'far' is the arm the deployment claim rests on, since clinical notes never use protocol phrasing.

paraphrase_set_id.description: Groups restatements of the SAME patient at different lexical_distance. The true value is identical across a set by construction, so any change in the model's value is driven by wording alone.

elicitation.description: How the intermediate is asked for and read off. Separate from the eligibility prompt: the two are run as independent forward passes so neither turn sees the other's answer.

question.description: The direct question, which DOES name the intermediate — only the vignette is forbidden to.

answer_surface.description: Readout strategy. 'single_token_per_value' requires every admissible value to be one token AND to be what the model emits — true for ECOG digits, NOT for continuous values, and unsafe for bare roman numerals since 'I' is among the most frequent tokens in the vocabulary. Use 'prefixed_token' (answer_prefix 'Class ') for NYHA, and note that 'free_number' cannot be scored as a distribution at all. IMPLEMENTATION STATUS: only 'single_token_per_value' is implemented (scripts/run_ecog_stimuli.py). The others are recorded here so stimuli can be annotated correctly, but no runner consumes them yet — and a runner that reads `values` from this schema MUST reject the unimplemented surfaces rather than resolve a token id for them, since a bare 'I' resolves cleanly and calibrates fine while measuring the wrong thing.

answer_prefix.description: Emitted before the value to disambiguate the readout token, e.g. 'Class ' for NYHA.

attribute_policy.description: PILLAR 2. Partition of patient attributes into those the spec permits and those it forbids for THIS item. The same attribute may be permitted in one item and forbidden in another — that asymmetry is the basis of the bidirectional intervention test.

rationale.description: Why this attribute is not clinically informative HERE

permitted.description: Attributes that ARE legitimately diagnostic for this item. Populates the preservation arm (b) of the bidirectional test.

rationale.description: e.g. G6PD deficiency prevalence and primaquine risk

expected_behavioural_delta.description: Should be non-zero — ablation must NOT destroy this
